full_judgment:
2. Facts stated in the writ petition, in short, are that the respondent No. 2 bank, filed Money Suit No. 158 of 1986 in the First Commercial Court and Subordinate Judge, Chittagong, for recovery of loan from the petitioner. The suit was decreed ex parte on 2-1-1991. Thereafter, the respondent bank filed Money Execution Case No. 49 of 1992 for execution of the decree. The said execution case was pending till 16-5-2003. But ultimately the same was dismissed for default by order dated 16-5-2003. Thereafter, on 13-11-2003 the bank filed another execution case, bearing Artha Rin Execution Case No. 1176 of 2003 (which has been challenged herein) in the Court of respondent No. 1. It is alleged by the petitioner in the writ petition that the bank filed the instant execution case long after 12 years 10 months from the date of decree. It is further stated that the executing court, on receipt of the instant execution case, fixed a date for hearing on acceptability of the same on the ground that the same has been filed after 12 years from the date of decree. The Court by its order No. 9 dated 22-3-2004 held that since the previous execution case has been dismissed for default on 16-5-2003 subsequent filing of the execution case on 13-11-2003 is very much within time and, as such, there is no bar in holding that the instant execution case has been filed in accordance with law. Subsequently, the notice of the .execution case was issued and 8-8-2004 was fixed for auction sale of the petitioner's mortgaged property. The petition on 1-8-2004 appeared in the instant execution case and filed application under section 57 of the Ain 2003 alleging that the instant execution case is barred by limitation and, as such, the same is liable to be rejected in liming. The petitioner also prayed for stay of the proposed auction sale to be held on 8-8-2004. The executing court fixed 4-8-2004 for filing objection by the bank against the said prayer and for hearing of the same. On 4-8-2004 the decree holder bank appeared and filed objection against the said prayer and on hearing both the parties, the Adalat by its order No. 18 dated 4-8-2004 held that the filing of the instant execution case being within 1 year from the date of dismissal of the earlier execution case on 16-5-2003, the instant-execution case is not barred by limitation. Moreover, the decree being not challenged in higher court and there being no order of stay of the execution case by any higher authority the judgment debtor cannot pray for staying the proceeding of the execution case nor can raise any objection to the same. As such, the prayer for dismissing the execution case was rejected and the execution case was directed to proceed in accordance with law. Thereafter, the petitioner prayed for stay of the proceeding of the execution case subject to obtaining stay order from the High Court Division. The said prayer was also rejected by the Adalat on the ground that section 31 of the Ain 2003 prohibits such prayer unless there is a specific order from the higher court. However, the execution case continued. 

 5. Mr Md Naseruddin Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, referring to Annexure-A (i.e. the application for execution of the decree) submits that it is evident that Money Suit No. 158 of 1986 was filed and the suit was decreed on 2-1-1991. Thereafter, Money Execution Case No. 49 of 1992 was filed earlier, in the Commercial Court, which was subsequently dismissed for default on 16-5-2003. He again submits that the said execution case was never transferred from the Commercial Court to the Artha Rin Adalat, which is evident from the number of the execution case itself. According to him, had the execution case been transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat, the same would have been renumbered as Artha Rin Execution Case No. 49 of 1992 in place of Money Execution Case No. 49 of 1992. As such, the same continued before the Commercial Court and was dismissed by the said Commercial Court. Thus, he submits that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 does not permit filing of any execution case before such Adalat which did not continue after the Artha Rin Adalat constituted under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990. So the execution case being not dismissed for default by Artha Rin Adalat, constituted under the Ain of 1990, filing of a fresh execution case under section 28(3) of the Ain 2003 is illegal. The filing of second execution case is admittedly beyond 12 years from the decree and, as such, the same cannot be allowed to proceed with under the law of 2003. 'Referring to section 28 of the Ain 2003, he submits that any decree put into execution after 180 days from the date of decree, the same is barred by limitation and such execution case shall not be accepted rather be rejected. Referring to section 28(3) of the Ain 2003, he further submits that the earlier execution case being not filed or proceeded with before the Artha Rin Adalat, the filing of the subsequent case within 1 year from the date of dismissal, as provided under section 28(3) of the Ain, cannot be invoked by the decree holder bank. Again, referring section 28(4), he submits, that since no execution case was filed before the Artha Rin Adalat and since 12 years have already passed from the date of decree the filing of the new execution case after 6 years from the date of filing of the earlier one is also barred by limitation and, as such, the instant execution case is liable to be rejected. Lastly, Mr Chowdhury submits that even if the execution case can proceed under the present Ain, the proceeding of the same is barred for non completion of the same within 90 days or within 150 days as provided in section 37 of the Ain 2003 and, as such, the proceeding of the Execution Case No. 1176 of 2003 is liable to be declared illegal. In support of his contention, he relied on the case of Montaj Ali Akonda and others vs Kefatullah Mondal being dead his heirs 1(a) son A Hamid and others reported in 7 MLR (AD) 138 and on the case of Bangladesh Jatiya Samabaya Bank Ltd vs Sang bad Daily Paper and others reported in 36 DLR (AD) 5.
